title: The Maker's Marks
summary: A second set of lot tiles carries Bjorn's hammer and pine. Bjorn's own card counts every tile he ever cast, and none to spare.
question: Whose hands poured the spare set of tiles in Gregor's strongbox?

clues.note: The spare set: the same grey iron as the chapel's, the same square letters, Bjorn's hammer and pine on every back.
Bjorn's mould, and below his card a tally of how many tiles he cast each year: one for every name the council counted, and no more.
Davin, the smith's boy, with a smith's shoulders gone thin.
DAVIN, cut in the seam with a line struck through it and the word RAN.

bjorn.reason: Bjorn's card counts every tile he cast, one to a name. He did not make a spare set, and he never knew there was one.

gregor.reason: Gregor kept the tiles in his strongbox. Kept is not poured. Who had the run of Bjorn's forge and knew his mould?

elena.reason: She recut one tile with an unpractised hand. Whoever poured these knew a mould.

mira.reason: Nothing in the iron says a tavern keeper's hand was ever near Bjorn's mould.

mathias.reason: The elder holds the urn's key, not a smith's ladle.

hints.text: The mark on the back means Bjorn's mould. Bjorn's tally means Bjorn's hand did not fill it twice.
A mould needs a hot forge and someone who knows it. Who learned that forge at Bjorn's side?

accuses: the spare lot tiles in Gregor's strongbox
solved_summary: matched the spare lot tiles to Bjorn's mould and worked out that his apprentice Davin poured them
